**SECTION D: ESSAY (10 MARKS).** Write an essay of 250 to 300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 1.** Imagine you are the Director of Preventive Medicine in Yaoundé. Propose to the Minister of Health a plan to eradicate malaria in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC sanctionne autant le respect du format imposé (note administrative structurée en propositions concrètes, récit narratif à la première personne, essai argumentatif « for or against ») que le contenu. Une proposition de plan sanitaire à un ministre doit rester concrète et organisée en mesures distinctes, pas un vague vœu pieux ; un récit doit suivre une progression chronologique claire avec un début, un problème et une résolution ; un essai « for or against » exige une position personnelle nette étayée par des arguments, tout en reconnaissant honnêtement les mérites de l'autre camp. Comme le sujet propose un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun l'un des formats possibles.

## Topic 1 - Proposal to the Minister (modèle, environ 270 mots)

Honourable Minister,

As Director of Preventive Medicine, I am submitting the following plan to accelerate the eradication of malaria in Cameroon, building on lessons learned from both successful and failed strategies elsewhere.

First, I propose a nationwide distribution of insecticide-treated mosquito nets, prioritising rural areas and households with young children and pregnant women, who remain the most vulnerable to severe complications. Distribution alone will not suffice; we must pair it with a public awareness campaign explaining correctly how and why these nets should be used every night, since a net left unused in a corner saves no one.

Second, I recommend stronger regulation of the informal drug market, where diluted or counterfeit anti-malarial medicines currently allow the parasite to develop resistance rather than be eliminated. Licensed pharmacies and community health workers should become the only authorised distributors of treatment, with real penalties for illegal street sales.

Third, I propose training and equipping community health workers in every district to diagnose and treat straightforward cases quickly and free of charge, reducing the number of patients who currently self-medicate improperly due to distance or cost barriers to formal healthcare.

Finally, given the environmental concerns that have limited DDT use elsewhere, I suggest investing instead in controlled larvicide programmes targeting stagnant water sources near settlements, combined with community-led clean-up efforts, an approach that reduces mosquito breeding grounds without the environmental drawbacks of widespread DDT spraying.

None of these measures alone will eradicate malaria, but implemented together and sustained over several years, they represent a realistic path towards dramatically reducing the burden this disease continues to place on Cameroonian families.

Respectfully submitted.

**SECTION D: ESSAY (10 MARKS).** Write an essay of 250 to 300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 2.** Tell your father a story in which you helped your friend who was very ill.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Narrative composition (modèle, environ 260 mots)

Dad, I have to tell you about something that happened last month, because I am still proud of how it turned out.

My friend Biya had been unusually quiet at school for days, and one afternoon she finally admitted she had been running a high fever for almost a week but was too afraid to tell her parents, since they were already struggling to pay her school fees and she did not want to add a hospital bill on top of that.

I could see she was getting weaker by the day, so I decided I could not simply wait and hope she would recover on her own. I walked with her to my aunt, who works as a nurse nearby, and explained the situation honestly. My aunt examined her immediately and became very concerned, saying the fever and the way Biya described her symptoms strongly suggested malaria that needed urgent treatment before it got worse.

Together, we convinced Biya to let my aunt contact her mother, who came rushing to the clinic once she understood how serious it actually was. My aunt helped arrange a reduced consultation fee, and Biya finally received the treatment she needed.

A week later, Biya was back at school, visibly relieved and much healthier. She told me afterwards that she had genuinely been scared to say anything, and that having someone simply notice and refuse to look away made all the difference.

I am telling you this, Dad, because I remembered what you always say: that real friendship sometimes means gently pushing someone towards help they are too afraid to ask for themselves.

**SECTION D: ESSAY (10 MARKS).** Write an essay of 250 to 300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 3.** Traditional healers are better than medical doctors. Put up your arguments for or against this statement.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Argumentative essay: for or against (modèle, environ 280 mots)

Whether traditional healers are better than medical doctors is a question that, in my view, has no single correct answer, since each brings something genuinely valuable that the other often lacks.

Those who favour traditional healers point out that they are usually more accessible, both geographically and financially, especially in rural communities where the nearest hospital may be hours away and consultation fees remain out of reach for many families. Traditional healers also treat patients within a familiar cultural framework, addressing not only physical symptoms but also the social and spiritual concerns that matter deeply to many patients, something modern medical consultations rarely have time to explore.

However, medical doctors offer something traditional healers generally cannot: treatments and diagnoses based on rigorously tested scientific evidence, capable of identifying and treating diseases like malaria, tuberculosis or diabetes with a precision and reliability that herbal remedies alone cannot consistently guarantee. Modern medicine has also produced vaccines and surgical techniques that have saved countless lives in ways traditional practice never could on its own.

I do not believe this means one must be declared universally "better" than the other. For a broken bone, a bacterial infection, or a serious disease like malaria, I would trust a qualified doctor without hesitation. For certain chronic conditions, or for the psychological and community support that accompanies healing in many of our cultures, a traditional healer's approach can offer something a hurried hospital consultation often cannot.

Rather than choosing one over the other, I believe Cameroon would benefit most from encouraging genuine collaboration between both traditions, each contributing what it does best to the health of our communities.

### Piège à éviter
Sur ce sujet, défendre une seule position sans reconnaître aucun mérite au camp opposé, alors que la consigne autorise explicitement un plaidoyer « for or against », affaiblit la crédibilité de l'argumentation si aucune limite du camp choisi n'est jamais admise.

### Conseil
Même sur un essai qui prend clairement position, mentionner honnêtement au moins un mérite réel du camp opposé renforce ta crédibilité aux yeux du correcteur, qui perçoit une réflexion nuancée plutôt qu'un parti pris non examiné.
